study: Five-case same skad3diag diagnostic APK matched camera/config study; native and ANGLE paired independently

window.method: Last complete loaded-scene contiguous camera tail; final30s by cumulative RenderBegin intervals

sf_presentation.one_percent_low_definition: 1000 / arithmetic mean of slowest ceil(0.01*N) present intervals; N>=100 required

interpretation.confirmed_submission_change: Both backends reduce median detail submissions86768 to3944, retain sun2958, and remove roughly2800 draws. The optimization is active in both; ANGLE OFF is genuinely unculled.
interpretation.native_result: Native ON repeats near37FPS versus16.64OFF in this scene; active render-thread CPU and local-light wall/elapsed stages fall.
interpretation.angle_result: ANGLE ON gain is only the measured ANGLE pair, about8percent, not the native2.2x ratio. Baseline ANGLE already submits the unculled workload with much lower CPU stage cost than baseline Native.
interpretation.mechanism_limit: The data do not identify the particular ANGLE batching/driver/synchronization implementation responsible for its cheaper unculled path. GPU timestamps include elapsed queue time and possible CPU-submission starvation.
interpretation.acceptance_limit: Performance evidence does not by itself establish pixel equality, final normal-build speed, long-duration stability, power savings or universal gains.

qualifications: GPU/CPU windows are independent final stable30s tails; SurfaceFlinger capture is its own30s window. No absolute timestamp alignment between them is claimed.
GPU timestamps sample every32frames and may include command starvation/waits on the GPU timeline; they are not a pure shader-busy or utilization measurement.
CPU stage values are wall elapsed scopes; active render thread CPU covers only the render window, excluding game/AI/physics outside it.
Inclusive stages overlap: do not add details to main/sun/local or bloom/luminance to combine.
Both runs report thermalstatus0 but ON starts and ends warmer; GPU devfreq snapshots differ. No equal-clock/equal-thermal or sustained frequency comparison is established.
The first A/B pair shows a presentation and submission-cost difference with matching camera/config. It does not alone prove visual identity, long-run thermal efficiency or an all-backend gain.
Only incomplete final JSON line is dropped if present; no complete performance record is discarded as an outlier. Camera/loading transients are excluded by explicit contiguous-tail rule.

Extra grass outside local shadow frusta is commonly clipped before fragment work; removal saves draw/vertex/uniform preparation and can relieve driver waits. Do not label removed local-light elapsed time as pure fragment overdraw.
Native ON1/ON2 provide a repeated presentation/submission result; a single ANGLE ON run does not establish a definitive backend ranking.
Device timestamps are exposed through different implementations/counter widths (Native40bit, ANGLE48bit); compare sampled elapsed stage intervals cautiously.
No power, energy-per-frame or thermal reduction is derived from these runs. Higher FPS changes work per second.
ANGLE OFF is now available and paired with ANGLE ON. Their measured gain must be reported separately from Native.
Native and ANGLE have different unculled CPU/driver behavior despite similar geometry counts. Avoid transferring a native percentage to ANGLE.
These are instrumented skad3diag runs. A later normal GPU-profiler-OFF/default-ON APK is not represented by this aggregate.
